content.text: {"platform":"linux","edition":"server","summary":{"total":38,"detects":0,"partial":25,"none":13,"coveredButOff":1},"techniques":[{"id":"T1685","name":"Disable or Modify Tools","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["ebpfHeartbeat","criticalPathFim"],"blindSpot":"Only the Falco alert path is probed, and only while a Falco unit is running (every ebpf_heartbeat_interval_secs; a second miss in a row is reported); the daemon does not watch its own other guards, and stopping the daemon itself is not reported by it. Blocking of other telemetry such as syslog forwarding or journald is not checked (blocking indicators, formerly T1562.006).","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1686","name":"Disable or Modify System Firewall","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The daemon re-creates its own tables every 30 seconds or so after a flush, but that is self-repair of its own rules: a change to the host's firewall is neither watched nor reported.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1685.004","name":"Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The Linux audit system is not read or protected: stopping auditd, auditctl -e 0 and deleting audit rules are not watched (only emptying audit.log is caught, see T1685.006).","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1685.006","name":"Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["logTamperWatch"],"blindSpot":"wtmp and btmp are checked by a hash of every 1 MiB block of their first 256 MiB (they only ever grow), kept on disk across restarts, so a record zeroed or edited in place is seen even when the size does not change or the daemon was down when it happened. lastlog is read record by record: a user's record that is emptied, set back to an earlier time or edited under the same time is reported. Does not see edits to wtmp/btmp after their first 256 MiB, edits to lastlog records of users that are not in /etc/passwd, or another log emptied and refilled to its old size between two checks.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1070.003","name":"Indicator Removal: Clear Command History","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"Shell history files are not watched. The exec recorder keeps its own hash-chained record of executed commands, so clearing the history does not erase what ran, but the clearing itself is not reported.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1070.004","name":"Indicator Removal: File Deletion","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder","criticalPathFim"],"blindSpot":"Only running a program from a deleted file (EXR-002) and the deletion of files on the critical-path list are reported; deleting any other file is not.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1574.006","name":"Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["criticalPathFim","execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Changes to /etc/ld.so.preload and the linker configuration are caught (and the next program run after such a change, EXR-007). LD_PRELOAD or LD_AUDIT naming a library outside the system directories, or LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at a writable directory, is caught when a service, or a service account, starts a program (EXR-013). Replaced shared libraries, and the environment of a process that was already running, are not seen.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1048","name":"Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"A command that an AI coding agent (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, aider, goose, cursor-agent, openclaw, qwen, crush) starts as a child process and that sends a credential file or a secret value out (curl with -T or -d, scp or rsync to a remote host, rclone, aws s3 cp, nc and the like) is reported (EXR-014), and so is a send within five minutes of a command of the same agent reading credential files (EXR-015). Only commands the agent starts as child processes are seen: the agent's own file reads, what it sends to its model provider, git push and connections that a script runtime opens itself are not, and neither is an agent whose process name is node. Notify-only.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1036","name":"Masquerading","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"Process names, paths and file names that imitate system ones are not checked.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1055","name":"Process Injection","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["yamaMemoryProtect"],"blindSpot":"Yama restricts ptrace between unrelated processes only on kernels that have it active; writes through /proc/<pid>/mem, LD_PRELOAD and other injection methods are neither prevented nor detected. The only injection report is a debugger attached by a service account (T1055.008).","liveState":"off"},{"id":"T1055.008","name":"Process Injection: Ptrace System Calls","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Only gdb, strace or ltrace started with a process id by a service account, or by a non-root user under a service process, is reported (EXR-012); other tools, root, and ordinary login sessions are not, and the attach itself is not watched, only the command line at start.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1027","name":"Obfuscated Files or Information","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder","containerExecGuard"],"blindSpot":"Only decode-and-run one-liners (EXR-004) and programs executed inside containers are matched against signatures; packed or encrypted payloads on the host pass.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1620","name":"Reflective Code Loading","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Only an exec from an anonymous memory file (memfd) is caught (EXR-002); code loaded into memory by a program that is already running, without a new exec, is not seen.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1543.002","name":"Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["criticalPathFim"],"blindSpot":"Only /etc/systemd/system is watched: user units (~/.config/systemd/user) and package unit directories are not.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1053.003","name":"Scheduled Task/Job: Cron","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["criticalPathFim","execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"The per-user crontabs in /var/spool/cron are not on the server's watch list; the Client Edition's persistence watch covers them.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1546.004","name":"Event Triggered Execution: Unix Shell Configuration Modification","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["criticalPathFim"],"blindSpot":"Only the folder /etc/profile.d and the file /etc/environment are watched: the start-up files in home folders (~/.bashrc and the like) and /etc/profile are not.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1546.018","name":"Event Triggered Execution: Python Startup Hooks","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"Python start-up files are not watched.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1546.017","name":"Event Triggered Execution: Udev Rules","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"No udev rules folder is watched.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1546.016","name":"Event Triggered Execution: Installer Packages","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"No package-manager hook folder is watched.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1546","name":"Event Triggered Execution (git hooks)","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"No git hook folder is watched in the Server Edition.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1037.004","name":"Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: RC Scripts","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"/etc/rc.local and the boot and login script folders are not watched.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1548.001","name":"Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["suidWatch"],"blindSpot":"A mode change is seen as it happens (FAN_ATTRIB on the local filesystems), with the process that made it, but a bit that is cleared again before the event is read, files inside container image layers, and changes while a package manager is running are left to the scan (default every 600 seconds), which sees only the state at that moment.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1098.004","name":"Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["criticalPathFim"],"blindSpot":"Only authorized_keys and authorized_keys2 in the .ssh folder of login accounts and /root/.ssh are watched; keys in a location set by sshd's AuthorizedKeysFile, or served by AuthorizedKeysCommand, are not.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1552.001","name":"Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["honeytokens"],"blindSpot":"Only decoy credential files are watched: a read of the real credential files is not reported.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1486","name":"Data Encrypted for Impact","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["ransomwareCanaryGuard","entropyWatch"],"blindSpot":"Decoy files trip only when touched. The entropy watch reads the head of files written in the watched folders only (the document roots, /var/www, /srv, the standard data folders of MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB and Redis, or entropy_watch_dirs), at most entropy_watch_max_files_per_sec files per second, so encryption elsewhere, slower than 20 files in 5 seconds from one writer, or of blocks as small as 16 bytes is not seen. A file written to a temporary name and renamed over an existing one in a watched folder is judged too, but a ciphertext put in place by a separate cp or mv command is not counted. By default it only notifies; it stops the writer only when entropy_watch_freeze is on.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1490","name":"Inhibit System Recovery","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Only btrfs subvolume delete and lvremove run by something other than a known snapshot manager are recognized (EXR-008); other ways of removing recovery points, such as deleting backup files, are not.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1071.004","name":"Application Layer Protocol: DNS","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["dnsTunnelDetect"],"blindSpot":"Heuristic and notify-only: bursts of long, high-entropy labels or TXT/NULL queries (10 within 60 seconds); slow or low-entropy tunnels and DNS over HTTPS are not seen.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1590.002","name":"Gather Victim Network Information: DNS","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["dnsTunnelDetect"],"blindSpot":"Notify-only: 40 different names under one domain that all come back NXDOMAIN within 60 seconds, seen in the UDP replies this host receives. Replies over TCP, DNS over HTTPS or TLS, queries from containers in their own network namespace, and slow enumeration are not seen.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1552.005","name":"Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["metadataWatch"],"blindSpot":"Cannot tell a forged request from a program that legitimately asks the metadata service. With Falco, the bundled rule names the process, its pid and its parent, and reports a root process too (only the cloud vendors' agents running as root are left out). Without Falco the firewall log names the account only, and root is not logged.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1059.004","name":"Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["reverseShellWatch","execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"A finding needs two scans in a row, and private-range peers are watched only when opted in. A shell whose standard input and output are not one outbound TCP or UDP connection is matched only when it is wired both ways to an interpreter, openssl, telnet, ssh or a relay tool that holds the connection and does not listen (always reported as a warning, never contained); a relay through a third program such as cat is not matched. The exec recorder (EXR-011) also reports known command-line shapes at start, which does not cover a shell started any other way.","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1505.003","name":"Server Software Component: Web Shell","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["webRulesWatch","execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"A web shell file is found when it is written to a watched document root (those in the Apache, nginx and Caddy settings and Docker mounts, and the folders set by the operator) and its content matches a web rule. A file is read whole up to 64 MiB (in chunks, at a low priority, with a cap per minute; the Client's on-access check up to 16 MiB), a bigger one by its first and last 1 MiB (the periodic scan: 4 MiB each), and an image by its first and last MiB, so a shell appended to an image is seen but code in the middle of a file bigger than 64 MiB is not; one that is obfuscated past the rules, or written outside those folders, is not either. A shell that runs code inside the web server process without a file is seen only when it starts a shell or interpreter one-liner from a service process (EXR-001).","liveState":"unknown"},{"id":"T1068","name":"Exploitation for Privilege Escalation","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Only a process seen with uid 0 and no setuid binary or capability in its ancestry is flagged (EXR-005); an exploit that never starts a process after gaining root is not seen.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1105","name":"Ingress Tool Transfer","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["execRecorder"],"blindSpot":"Only curl|sh style pipes and a downloaded file executed within the time window (default 120 seconds) are linked (EXR-003), for curl, wget and tnftp/ftp with -o, including combined flags such as curl -fsSLo and wget -qO; a download that is run later, or fetched by another client, is not.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1110.001","name":"Brute Force: Password Guessing","platform":"linux","coverage":"partial","coveredBy":["sshGuard"],"blindSpot":"Follows sshd's log only: guessing against other services is not counted. A lost journal cursor, a truncated log or a log that cannot be read leaves a gap that liveState and the collectors record show; with no readable log nothing is banned.","liveState":"on"},{"id":"T1557.002","name":"Adversary-in-the-Middle: ARP Cache Poisoning","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The Server Edition does not watch the ARP table.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1557.003","name":"Adversary-in-the-Middle: DHCP Spoofing","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The Server Edition does not watch DHCP leases or network settings.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1557.001","name":"Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The Server Edition does not watch for forged LLMNR, NBNS or mDNS answers or for proxy auto-configuration; its security report only shows whether this host has an LLMNR or NBNS responder bound.","liveState":"not_applicable"},{"id":"T1195.001","name":"Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools","platform":"linux","coverage":"none","coveredBy":[],"blindSpot":"The Server Edition runs no automatic npm check (install-time code, look-alike dependency names); its lockfile change watch is not counted in this map.","liveState":"not_applicable"}],"guards":[{"id":"ebpfHeartbeat","state":"unknown"},{"id":"criticalPathFim","state":"unknown"},{"id":"logTamperWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"execRecorder","state":"on"},{"id":"yamaMemoryProtect","state":"off"},{"id":"containerExecGuard","state":"unknown"},{"id":"suidWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"honeytokens","state":"unknown"},{"id":"ransomwareCanaryGuard","state":"unknown"},{"id":"entropyWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"dnsTunnelDetect","state":"unknown"},{"id":"metadataWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"reverseShellWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"webRulesWatch","state":"unknown"},{"id":"sshGuard","state":"on"}],"caveats":["This is a self-check of what RoamSwitch watches. A partial entry states what it does not see in blindSpot, none means nothing looks for the technique, and a technique that is not listed was not assessed.","liveState is on when the guard is enabled in the settings and its daemon is running, off when it is disabled or the daemon is not running, and unknown when it could not be read. Client Edition settings are read from the invoking user's config.json, which can differ from the copy the daemon reads. A guard that is switched on but known for certain not to work (a missing tool, a refused kernel feature, a dead helper) is shown off or partial, with the reason in `inactive`.","The RoamSwitch OS image adds detectors of its own (auditd rules, a self-test per technique). This map covers the standalone Client and Server Editions.","The other edition is the one installed on this host. The settings and daemon of the edition asked for are read, so liveState tends to be off or unknown."]}
